source.title: Open problems on countable dense homogeneity

accepted.question_text: A separable space X is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if, for every two countable dense subsets D and E of X, there is a homeomorphism f from X onto X such that f[D] = E. A space is strongly locally homogeneous (SLH) if it has a basis B such that, whenever x and y lie in the same U in B, some autohomeomorphism of X sends x to y and is the identity outside U. Is every connected CDH metric space SLH?
accepted.context_brief: connected CDH metric spaces and SLH

evidence.quote: A separable space X is countable dense homogeneous (CDH) if, given any two countable dense subsets D and E of X, there is a homeomorphism f : X → X such that f[D] = E.

Recall that a space X is strongly local ly homogeneous [34] if it has a basis B of open sets such that for every U ∈ B and every x, y ∈ U there is an autohomeomorphism h of X such that h(x) = y and h restricts to the identity on X \ U.
Problem 1. Is every connected CDH metric space SLH?
The problem was finally solved by van Mill [66].

accepted.question_text: For a metric continuum, where CDH means that any two countable dense subsets can be carried onto each other by a self-homeomorphism, is every CDH metric continuum strongly locally homogeneous (SLH)?

evidence.quote: An important special case of Problem 1 remains unsolved.
Problem 1’. Is every CDH metric continuum SLH?

accepted.question_text: If X is a countable dense homogeneous metric space and U is an open subspace of X, must U itself be countable dense homogeneous?
accepted.context_brief: open subspaces of CDH metric spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 2. If X is CDH and metric and U is open in X, must U be CDH?
Problem 2 and the first part of Problem 2’ were answered by van Mill [67]: there is a CDH Polish space with a dense connected open subset that is rigid.

accepted.question_text: If X is a connected countable dense homogeneous metric space and U is an open connected subspace of X, must U be homogeneous, meaning that any two points of U can be mapped to one another by a self-homeomorphism of U?

evidence.quote: Problem 2’. If X is connected, CDH, and metric, and U is an open, connected set in X, must U be homogeneous?
Problem 2 and the first part of Problem 2’ were answered by van Mill [67]: there is a CDH Polish space with a dense connected open subset that is rigid.

accepted.question_text: If X is a connected countable dense homogeneous metric space, U is an open connected subspace of X, and U is homogeneous, must U be countable dense homogeneous?
accepted.context_brief: CDH status of homogeneous open connected subspaces

evidence.quote: If U is homogeneous, is it necessarily CDH?
To recapitulate: Problems 1, 2, 2’ (first part), 4 (first part), 6 and 6’ are solved, while parts of Problems 2’, and 4 (second part), and Problems 1’, 3, and 5 remain open.

accepted.question_text: If X is a connected Polish space that is countable dense homogeneous, must X be locally connected?
accepted.context_brief: local connectedness of connected Polish CDH spaces

evidence.quote: Problem 3. If X is a CDH, connected, Polish space, must X be locally connected?

accepted.question_text: For zero-dimensional subsets X of the real line R, characterize when the countable power X^omega is homogeneous.

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For which 0-dimensional subsets X of R is Xω homogeneous? CDH?
The first part of this problem was answered by Lawrence [55], and further extended by Dow and Pearl [21]

accepted.question_text: For zero-dimensional subsets X of the real line R, characterize when the countable power X^omega is countable dense homogeneous.
accepted.context_brief: CDH countable powers of zero-dimensional real subspaces

evidence.quote: Problem 4. For which 0-dimensional subsets X of R is Xω homogeneous? CDH?
The second part of the question is still being investigated though important partial results were obtained:

accepted.question_text: Is the countable power of the Niemytzki plane homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 5. Is the ωth power of the Niemytzki plane homogeneous?
Observe that the Niemytzki plane is not metrizable. This problem is open.

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a countable dense homogeneous metric space that is not Polish?

evidence.quote: Problem 6. Does there exist a CDH metric space that is not Polish?
Both Problems 6 and 6’ were solved in the affirmative by Farah, Hrušák and Martínez Ranero [25].

accepted.question_text: Is there an absolute example of a countable dense homogeneous metric space whose cardinality is aleph_1?
accepted.context_brief: absolute CDH metric space of size aleph_1

evidence.quote: Problem 6’. Is there an absolute example of a CDH metric space of cardinality ω1?
Both Problems 6 and 6’ were solved in the affirmative by Farah, Hrušák and Martínez Ranero [25].

accepted.question_text: Is every locally compact connected countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous, and more generally is every compact connected countable dense homogeneous space strongly locally homogeneous?
accepted.context_brief: compact connected CDH spaces and SLH

evidence.quote: Problem 7. Is every (locally) compact connected CDH-space SLH?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a connected metrizable countable dense homogeneous space that is not strongly 2-homogeneous, where strongly 2-homogeneous means that any two ordered pairs of distinct points can be matched coordinatewise by a self-homeomorphism?
accepted.context_brief: connected metric CDH spaces not strongly 2-homogeneous

evidence.quote: The space X is strongly n-homogeneous if given two one-to-one sequences {ai : i < n}, {bi : i < n} of points in X both of length n, there is a homeomorphism h ∈ H (X) such that h(ai) = bi for every i < n.
He also presented an example of a connected CDH topological space which is not strongly 2-homogeneous and asked whether there is a metric example:
Problem 8 (van Mill [71]). Is there a connected CDH-space which is not strongly 2-homogeneous?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a locally compact countable dense homogeneous space that has a dense open subspace which is not countable dense homogeneous?

evidence.quote: Problem 9 (Ungar). Is there a locally compact CDH-space with a dense open non-CDH-subspace?

accepted.question_text: For a countable dense homogeneous continuum, must every open subspace also be countable dense homogeneous, homogeneous, or both?

evidence.quote: Problem 10 (Watson–Simon [94]). Are open subsets of CDH continua CDH? Homogeneous?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent with ZFC that there is a connected countable dense homogeneous subspace X of the plane R^2 that is meager-in-itself?

evidence.quote: Problem 11. Is there consistently a connected CDH X ⊆ R2 which is meager-in-itself?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent with ZFC that there is a crowded countable dense homogeneous subset X of the real line whose cardinality is less than the continuum c and which is a Baire space?
accepted.context_brief: small crowded Baire CDH sets of reals

evidence.quote: Problem 12. Is there consistently a crowded CDH set X ⊆ R of size less than c which is Baire?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Bernstein subset of the real line that is countable dense homogeneous, where a Bernstein subset of R is one whose set and complement both meet every Cantor set in R?

evidence.quote: A subset X of R is called Bernstein if X and R \ X intersect every Cantor set in R.
Problem 13 (Baldwin and Beaudoin [7]). Is there a Bernstein subset of R which is CDH?

accepted.question_text: Is there, in ZFC, a zero-dimensional countable dense homogeneous space X whose square X^2 is not countable dense homogeneous?
accepted.context_brief: zero-dimensional CDH spaces with non-CDH squares

evidence.quote: Problem 14 (Medini [58]). Is there (in ZFC) a zero-dimensional CDH space X such that X2 is not CDH?

accepted.question_text: For which natural numbers n does there exist a countable dense homogeneous space X such that every finite power X^i is countable dense homogeneous for i <= n, but X^(n+1) is not countable dense homogeneous?
accepted.context_brief: finite product threshold from CDH to non-CDH

evidence.quote: Problem 15 (Medini [58]). For which n ∈ ω is there a CDH space X such that Xi is CDH for all i ≤ n while Xn+1 is not CDH?

accepted.question_text: For which natural numbers n does there exist a space X such that X^i is not countable dense homogeneous for every i <= n, but X^(n+1) is countable dense homogeneous; and can such an X be chosen to be a continuum?
accepted.context_brief: finite product threshold from non-CDH to CDH

evidence.quote: Problem 16 (Medini [58]). For which n ∈ ω is there a CDH space X such that Xi is not CDH for all i ≤ n while Xn+1 is CDH? Can X be a continuum?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a zero-dimensional space X that is not countable dense homogeneous while its square X^2 is countable dense homogeneous, and can such an X be chosen to be rigid?

evidence.quote: Problem 17 (Medini [58]). Is there a zero-dimensional space X that is not CDH while X2 is CDH? Can X be rigid?

accepted.question_text: For the product phenomena in which powers of a space alternate between countable dense homogeneous and non-countable dense homogeneous behavior, can any of the spaces witnessing these phenomena be chosen to be definable, for example analytic or co-analytic?

evidence.quote: Medini [58] also raises the question whether any of such spaces can be definable (e.g. analytic or co-analytic).

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a non-meager P-filter?

evidence.quote: The following remains a major open problem in combinatorial set theory:
Problem 18. ([48]) Is there a non-meager P-filter?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that BA(R, aleph_3) holds, where BA(X,kappa) means that any two kappa-dense subsets A and B of X can be matched by a self-homeomorphism h of X with h[A] = B?

evidence.quote: Following [88] we denote by BA(X, κ) the formally weaker property that given two κ-dense subsets A, B of a space X there is a homeomorphism h ∈ H (X) such that h[A] = B.
Problem 19 (Baumgartner). Is BA(R, ℵ3) consistent?

accepted.question_text: For n,m > 1 and uncountable cardinals kappa and lambda, determine the implications among higher-dimensional kappa-CDH and BA properties: does R^n being omega_1-CDH imply R^m is omega_1-CDH; does BA(R^n,kappa) imply BA(R^n,lambda) when kappa > lambda; does BA(R,omega_1) imply BA(R^n,omega_1) for all n > 1; and does BA(R^n,kappa) imply that R^n is kappa-CDH? Here kappa-CDH means that any two indexed families of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets can be matched coordinatewise by a self-homeomorphism, while BA(X,kappa) means any two kappa-dense subsets of X can be matched by a self-homeomorphism.

evidence.quote: Inspired by this fact, let us call a space X κ-CDH if given two families {Aα : α<κ} and {Bα : α<κ} of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets there is a homeomorphism h ∈ H (X) such that h[Aα] = Bα for every α<κ.

Problem 20 (Stepr¯ans–Watson). (1) Does Rn being ω1-CDH imply that Rm is ω1-CDH for n, m > 1? (2) Does BA(Rn, κ) imply BA(Rn, λ) when κ > λ? (3) Does BA(R, ω1) imply BA(Rn, ω1) for all n > 1? (4) Does BA(Rn, κ) imply that Rn is κ-CDH for n > 1 and κ uncountable?

accepted.question_text: Is every Polish countable dense homogeneous space omega-CDH, meaning that any two countable indexed families of pairwise disjoint countable dense sets can be matched coordinatewise by a self-homeomorphism?

evidence.quote: Problem 21. Is every Polish CDH space ω-CDH?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Polish countable dense homogeneous space, or at least some countable dense homogeneous space, that is not 2-CDH?

evidence.quote: Problem 22 (Rubin). Is there a (Polish) space X which is CDH but not 2-CDH?

accepted.question_text: If a Polish space is 1/omega-CDH, meaning that it has exactly countably many equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms, must it contain a dense open countable dense homogeneous subspace?
accepted.context_brief: dense open CDH subspaces of Polish 1/omega-CDH spaces

evidence.quote: Call a topological space X 1 κ-CDH if there are exactly κ-many types of countable dense subsets of X, i.e. κ-many equivalence classes of the family of all countable dense sets of X modulo an equivalence relation
Problem 23. Does every Polish 1 ω -CDH space contain a dense open CDH subspace?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Polish space that is 1/2-CDH, meaning that it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms, and that has no dense open countable dense homogeneous subspace?
accepted.context_brief: Polish 1/2-CDH spaces without dense open CDH subspaces

evidence.quote: Problem 24. Is there a 1 2 -CDH Polish space without a dense open CDH subspace?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a homogeneous subset of the real line R that is 1/2-CDH, meaning that it has exactly two equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Problem 25. Is there a homogeneous 1 2 -CDH subset of R?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a Polish space, or even a locally compact space, that is 1/aleph_1-CDH, meaning that it has exactly aleph_1 equivalence classes of countable dense subsets under self-homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Problem 26. Is there a (Polish, locally compact) space which is 1 ω1 -CDH?

accepted.question_text: Is it consistent that there is a filter that is 1/kappa-CDH for some cardinal kappa strictly between 1 and the continuum c?

evidence.quote: Problem 27 (Kunen, Medini and Zdomskyy [53, Question 5]). Is it consistent that there exists a 1 κ -CDH filter for a cardinal κ such that 1 < κ < c?

accepted.question_text: For which cardinals kappa does there exist a zero-dimensional countable dense homogeneous space X such that the square X^2 is 1/kappa-CDH?

evidence.quote: Problem 28 (Medini [58]). For which cardinals κ is there a zero-dimensional CDH space X such that X2 is 1 κ-CDH?

accepted.question_text: Is the Hilbert cube, equipped with its standard metric, Lipschitz countable dense homogeneous, meaning that for every epsilon > 0 and every two countable dense subsets A and B there is an epsilon-almost isometry h with h[A] = B?

evidence.quote: They call a metric spaces X Lipschitz countable dense homogeneous (Lipschitz-CDH) if given ε > 0 and A, B countable dense subsets of E there is an ε-almost isometry h such that h[A] = B.
Problem 29 (Dijkstra [18]). Is the Hilbert cube with its standard metric Lipschitz-CDH?

evidence.quote: Problem 30 (Hernández–Hrušák–van Mill [43]). Is there (in ZFC) a compact CDH space of weight c?

accepted.question_text: Does there exist a compact countable dense homogeneous space that contains no copy of the Cantor set?
accepted.context_brief: compact CDH spaces without Cantor sets

evidence.quote: Problem 31. Is there a compact CDH-space which does not contain a copy of the Cantor set?

accepted.question_text: Is the cardinal invariant b the minimal possible weight of a separable non-countable-dense-homogeneous manifold; if not, is there a natural combinatorial characterization of that minimal weight?
accepted.context_brief: minimal weight of separable non-CDH manifolds

evidence.quote: Problem 33. Is b the minimal weight of a separable, non-CDH manifold?
If not, is there (as Watson asks) a nice combinatorial characterization of the minimal weight of a separable, non-CDH manifold?

trace.notes: Normalized the single URL input https://zbmath.org/6894002. A local shard entry identified the zbMATH record as Open problems on countable dense homogeneity with DOI 10.1016/j.topol.2018.03.023.

Resolved the zbMATH record through exact-title and DOI recovery. ScienceDirect exposed the same title and DOI as an open archive article, and the author-hosted final PDF at staff.fnwi.uva.nl matched the published title, journal, DOI, and page range, so it was used as the readable primary source.

Mapped the PDF structure: introduction and definitions on page 185; Fitzpatrick and Zhou problem review on pages 186-187; new and old problem list in subsections 3.1 through 3.8 on pages 188-194; references begin on page 194.
Extracted Problems 1, 1', 2, 2', 3, 4, 5, 6, and 6' from the review of Fitzpatrick and Zhou's problems; split mixed-status compound questions where one clause was solved and another remained open.
Extracted Problems 7-33 from subsections 3.1 through 3.8, including the definability question following Problem 17 and compound subquestions in Problems 16, 17, 20, and 33.

Rewrote each problem as a standalone question, expanding CDH, SLH, strongly n-homogeneous, kappa-CDH, BA(X,kappa), 1/kappa-CDH, Lipschitz-CDH, Bernstein set, and other local terminology only where supported by the PDF text.
Kept numbered problem statements distinct. Split only compound or mixed-status questions; no near-duplicate rewritten questions were merged.

Accepted all extracted items after checking that each has a page-numbered evidence quote, no source-pointing language in question_text, and solved-status metadata set true only where the PDF explicitly says the problem was answered or solved.
Saved exact JSON result to outputs/parse-paper/6894002.json and outputs/latest.json.
